steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Text-to-image makes new things. Inpainting fixes old ones. In production, 70% of billable image work is editing — swap a background, remove a logo, extend the canvas, regenerate a hand. Inpainting is where diffusion earns its keep.

steps.title: The problem
cards: A client sends a perfect product photo with a distracting sign in the background. You want to erase the sign and leave everything else pixel-identical. You cannot run text-to-image from scratch — the result will have a different color, different lighting, different product angle. You want to regenerate *only* the masked region, and you want the regeneration to respect the surrounding context.

- **Inpainting.** Regenerate inside a mask, keep outside pixels.
- **Outpainting.** Regenerate outside a mask (or beyond the canvas), keep inside.
- **Image editing.** Regenerate the whole image but keep semantic or structural fidelity to the original (SDEdit, InstructPix2Pix).
